authority: Original repertoire source moves and CC0 Lichess puzzle continuations; legal-source instructional targets, not universal engine-unique moves.

items.goal: Compare central control, development, and king safety before choosing a principled opening move.
items.misconception: A familiar opening move is not an automatic rule. First check the pawn structure and whose king needs safety.
items.hint: Identify the move that improves the position for a concrete reason, not because its notation is familiar.

items.goal: Find a productive development move that adds influence without surrendering material.
items.misconception: Moving a developed piece a second time can waste a tempo when an untouched minor piece needs work.
items.hint: Which undeveloped piece has the clearest useful square in this exact position?

items.goal: Find a legal move that contests or supports the center in this pawn structure.
items.misconception: Do not push a central pawn without checking its support and the opponent's pawn contacts.
items.hint: Count e4, d4, e5, and d5 attackers and pawn breaks before acting.

items.goal: Improve king safety or prepare a sound castling setup with natural development.
items.misconception: A kingside attacking plan is premature when the king and development lag behind.
items.hint: Which move helps secure your king while keeping the center defensible?

items.goal: Choose a useful developing or central move while the queen need not come out early.
items.misconception: Bringing the queen out before the minor pieces can donate tempi to attacks on the queen.
items.hint: Can a minor piece or pawn make the intended improvement without early queen exposure?

items.goal: Make progress with a move whose immediate purpose responds to the present position.
items.misconception: Do not confuse a forcing-looking move with a genuinely productive tempo.
items.hint: What does your move improve, threaten, or prevent—and what answer might your opponent have?

items.goal: Activate a piece on a useful square rather than making a purposeless move.
items.misconception: Activity is measured by influence and coordination, not by how far a piece travels.
items.hint: Which piece gains a useful file, diagonal, or central square after this move?

items.goal: Improve the currently least useful piece without creating a new weakness.
items.misconception: Repeatedly improving an already active piece leaves undeveloped teammates out of play.
items.hint: Find the least effective piece and name its next useful role before moving.

items.goal: Locate the move that threatens two vulnerable targets in the recorded puzzle line.
items.misconception: A move attacking only one piece may give the defender time to save everything.
items.hint: Identify two targets and calculate the defender's immediate resource.

items.goal: Look for a knight jump that attacks multiple valuable targets at once.
items.misconception: A geometrical fork is not a win if the knight can simply be taken or the targets can escape.
items.hint: Trace the knight's landing square and each target before committing.

items.goal: Find the source move that exploits a piece constrained by something behind it.
items.misconception: A pinned piece is not automatically immobile; check which moves are legal and what lies behind.
items.hint: Inspect the attacking ray and the higher-value piece behind the target.

items.goal: Force a valuable piece to move so a target behind it becomes available.
items.misconception: A skewer requires a genuine line of attack through the front piece.
items.hint: Find the line, the first target and what becomes exposed if it moves.

items.goal: Reveal an existing piece's line by moving its blocker with purpose.
items.misconception: Moving a blocker is not enough unless the revealed line creates a useful threat.
items.hint: Identify the rear attacker, the blocking piece and its destination.

items.goal: Remove or distract the unit that guards a critical target.
items.misconception: Capturing any available piece may leave the decisive defender intact.
items.hint: Find the defender's exact duty and the target that becomes vulnerable.

items.goal: Force a defender away from a square or piece it must protect.
items.misconception: A threat does not work if the defender can remain on its key square without consequence.
items.hint: Locate the defender's duty and a forcing reason it must abandon that duty.

items.goal: Lure an opponent's piece onto an unfavorable square before the follow-up.
items.misconception: The destination square matters: not every tempting sacrifice creates a tactical gain.
items.hint: Identify where the opposing piece is induced to go and what follows.

items.goal: Check the king's escape squares before choosing a back-rank attack.
items.misconception: An apparently trapped king may have a flight square or a timely defensive interposition.
items.hint: Verify escape squares and all forcing defenses before claiming mate.

items.goal: Expose a defender with two incompatible defensive responsibilities.
items.misconception: Two attacked targets are not enough if different pieces can defend each one.
items.hint: List both duties of the same defender and test whether one can be abandoned.

items.goal: Clear a square or line so another piece can execute the decisive follow-up.
items.misconception: The clearing move must actually release the needed square or line; moving randomly does not.
items.hint: Identify the piece blocking the tactic and the route it should vacate.
